answer: A clone earns its epoch only through the anchor of a cedar it runs on: the cedar's own signed hardware fingerprint, co-signed each epoch by its grove of neighbouring hosts after an on-site audit. A grove may co-sign no more anchors than the cedars its audit counted, forfeiting its locked stake whole if it signs past the count. So one operator's k fakes need k audited cedars — the k-th costs another physical machine bought and installed — while a newcomer buys one.
